newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Danny threatens Alabama, Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Danny threatens Alabama, Mississippi.

text.p: Hurricane Danny crept across the northern Gulf of Mexico on Friday after spending most of the day stalled off Louisiana, pounding the coast with gale-force winds and torrential rains.

Danny, a minimal hurricane, first made landfall along the tip of Louisiana earlier in the day, flooding highways and flattening power lines with winds gusting up to 100 miles an hour (160 kph) before stalling off the coast, officials said.

Hurricane warnings were up from Grand Isle, La., east to Destin, Fla., as the storm moved slowly away from the Louisiana coast into the open waters of the Gulf of Mexico. Rain extended east across the Florida panhandle.

"It's drifting northward now. We're looking for it to make landfall somewhere near the Mississippi-Alabama state line, probably about 9 a.m. Saturday," Jill Hasling, a meteorologist with private forecaster Weather Research Centre said.
The U.S. Coast Guard said rescuers in Panama City, Fla., were searching for a missing surfer and that two people disappeared in heavy seas off the coast of Biloxi, Miss.

The governors of Mississippi and Alabama issued a state of emergency ahead of the storm, which threatened to make landfall on Saturday packing an up to nine-foot (2.7 metre) storm surge. Twenty inches (51 cm) of rain were forecast over the weekend along the storm's track.

In Pascagoula, Miss., high winds and strong currents ripped an oil drilling rig from its berth and rammed it into a research vessel, tearing a hole in the ship's fuel tank and spilling 500 gallons of diesel fuel into the port.
The Coast Guard secured nearby ships while state officials oversaw a hasty cleanup effort.

"We closed the port at 5 a.m., which kept a number of ships stuck at port that had wanted to get out into the harbour and ride this (storm) out," said Melody Bradley, director of the Jackson County Port Authority.
Biloxi Police Chief Tommy Moffett said authorities were considering opening a shelter for a large number of stranded tourists at area beaches and casinos.

"Right now, it's just a matter of trying to get ready while we wait to see if there really is anything to get ready for," he said. "We know that with hurricanes, you just never know what's going to happen. Danny could come here, head east, or turn around and go back to Louisiana."

The Copa casino in Gulfport, Miss., one of 11 floating casinos operating along the Gulf Coast, was closed for a second day on Friday but state officials decided not to order the remaining barge casinos shuttered ahead of the storm.

Emergency officials from Mississippi east to the Florida panhandle urged coastal residents to move to higher ground ahead of the storm in voluntary evacuations that sent streams of cars heading inland.

On Friday afternoon, high winds, steady rain and wind-driven water bombarded Plaquemines Parish southeast of New Orleans, but roads were reopening about 12 hours after Hurricane Danny punched into the "toe" of Louisiana's boot-shaped coastline.

About 100 boats appeared to have been damaged or sunk at a large marina in Buras, La., where storm waters rose four to five feet (1.2 to 1.5 metres) within a few minutes earlier in the day. In nearby areas, house trailers were overturned, roofs blown off and trees and utility poles snapped, he said.

West of Plaquemines, officials in Grand Isle, Louisiana's only inhabited barrier island, reported heavy damage and erosion. Most of the island's 1,530 residents obeyed a mandatory evacuation order Thursday and moved inland.
In New Orleans, the storm's impact was limited to occasional showers and wind gusts as the city was spared the heavy rains that could have caused widespread flooding.

The storm first made landfall overnight between Grand Isle and the mouth of the Mississippi River. The eye of the hurricane at 4 p.m. CDT (5 p.m. EDT) was located about 65 miles (144 km) southwest of Mobile, near latitude 29.9 north, longitude 88.8 west.

Hurricane force winds of 75 miles an hour (120 kph) extended outward about 25 miles (40 km) from the centre, with the strongest gusts on the east side of the storm as it crept northeast at about 6 miles an hour (10 kph).
